neighbours.label: the first subword piece of a split adjective (often after a hyphen or comparative: less-ser|ious, time-p|oor, res|plendent), where the output predicts the adjective's completion
fire: Officials said a less-serious collision had happened on the same line last spring.
The planner offers a package for time-poor couples who cannot organise everything.
Older athletes are prone to more-severe injuries and need longer to recover.
The leaves are broadly elliptic-oblanceolate with a slightly wavy margin.
Peacocks are famous for their resplendent plumage and loud calls.
The hikers crossed an unforgiving, sun-scorched plateau before dusk.
Critics found the sequel overwrought and needlessly convoluted in places.
The shop sold slightly mismatched, semi-transparent glass beads.
quiet: Officials said a small collision had happened on the same line last spring.
The planner offers a package for busy couples who cannot organise everything.
Older athletes are prone to bad injuries and need longer to recover.
The leaves are broad and long with a slightly wavy margin.
Peacocks are famous for their bright plumage and loud calls.
The hikers crossed a hot, dry plateau before dusk.
Critics found the sequel long and slow in places.
The shop sold small, clear glass beads.

notes: card: no single token; peaks on word-internal pieces of adjectives; output promotes adjective words (noisy, risky, messy). Near misses use whole-token common adjectives in the same frames.
